turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Mr Naidoo's blood pressure is 146 over 88, and his pulse is seventy four. The machine in room two is on the blink, so I used this one.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, sister. Good morning, doctor. I hope this appointment is not an inconvenience.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not at all. Umm, one second, the screen has frozen. Right. What brings you in today?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I have come about the left hand, doctor. It is still slightly weak, three months after the mild stroke.
[SEG0005] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm Lindi, his wife. He drops the teaspoon at breakfast and then pretends nothing happened.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. The date on the file is blank. When was the stroke? Say it again for me.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Three months ago, doctor. I cannot recall the exact day. Possibly early May, though I would not swear to it.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Of. Any dizziness since then?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I have not felt dizzy at all.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain, or shortness of breath?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain, and no shortness of breath. My breathing is comfortable.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): How is the walking going?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): I walk to the robot and back each morning. It is a little slower than before, though I feel steady.
[SEG0014] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He holds my arm on the hill home. He gets tired, shame, even on that short bit.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): A little tired, yes, doctor. It is not severe.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tired on the hill. Sorry, I was typing. And the speech, has that come right?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): It has largely come right, doctor. Now and then a word will not come to me, for a second only.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me check the hand. Squeeze my fingers. Err, the left grip is weaker than the right. The face is symmetrical, no droop.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): This medication list is a proper mess. Aspirin, atorvastatin, amlodipine, Omprazole, Mizartan, Metformine. Which of these do you actually take?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I take aspirin each morning, atorvastatin at night, and one amlodipine tablet in the morning. I also take the Omprazole, twenty milligrams, for the heartburn.
[SEG0021] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The aspirin is a hundred milligrams. I pack his box every week. He will tell you it is seventy five.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): I was told seventy five milligrams, doctor. If the packet says otherwise, I cannot say which figure is correct.
[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The box at home says 100 mg. He still says 75. The chemist never settled it for us.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Of. Mizartan. Why is that sitting on the list?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Mizartan was for the pressure, doctor. It was stopped when the amlodipine was started. I have not taken it since.
[SEG0026] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Metformine is not his, doctor. Those are my sugar tablets. He never takes them.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Your Metformine, not his. Umm. What strength is the amlodipine tablet?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Five milligrams. One tablet every morning, for the blood pressure.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the atorvastatin. What dose, and do you actually take it?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Forty milligrams at night. I must admit I miss it on some evenings, once I am already in bed.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Omprazole, twenty milligrams. Is that every morning?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. Twenty milligrams each morning. It suits me. I have never had a reaction to it.
[SEG0033] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He also takes half a water tablet in the morning, the small white one, with the amlodipine. I do not know the proper name.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Half a water tablet, name unknown. Anything else? Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No other medicines, doctor. And no allergies whatsoever.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Forgive me, I ought to correct an earlier answer. I do become light-headed for a few seconds when I rise from the chair. It had slipped my mind.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Light-headed when you stand. Say that once more? Only a few seconds?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Only a few seconds, doctor, and only when I rise. If I wait, it passes. There is no spinning.

[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): I think the weak hand is residual from the stroke, not a fresh event. The light-headedness might be the blood pressure, though I cannot be sure. We will book bloods this week, the cholesterol and a kidney test.

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep the aspirin, the atorvastatin, try not to skip those nights, the amlodipine five milligrams, the Omprazole and the half water tablet. Come back in six weeks. If the hand suddenly worsens or the speech slurs, go straight to casualty, do not wait.
[SEG0041] person_1 (NURSE): I'll book those bloods for Thursday morning, Mr Naidoo, before the rooms fill up.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday morning is perfectly suitable. Thank you, sister. Thank you, doctor.

traps.happens: The transcript looks like speech-to-text: drug names are sometimes spelled wrongly ('Omprazole', 'Mizartan' for telmisartan, 'Metformine'), fragments and fillers appear ('Err', 'Of.', 'Mm.', 'Umm'), numbers are sometimes digits and sometimes words.
traps.label_rule: Medicine names are recorded as written in the transcript (name) with a normalized/generic name ONLY when the true drug is certain from context (a drug 'for the pressure' written 'Mizartan' is NOT certain enough: leave generic_name empty). Fragments and fillers are never facts.

features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
